findings.title: Missing `key` prop for Grafana-origin rule items in FilterView list
findings.body: In the `rules.map((ruleWithOrigin) => {...})` loop, the 'datasource' and default cases pass `key={key}` to their returned elements, but the 'grafana' case's `<GrafanaRuleListItem .../>` (previously `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../>`) no longer has a `key` prop set. Since React requires a stable `key` on elements returned directly from a `.map()` callback, this will produce 'Each child in a list should have a unique key prop' warnings and can cause incorrect DOM reuse/reconciliation when the filtered rule list updates (e.g. on refetch or pagination), potentially showing stale rule data for Grafana rules in the filtered/search view.

findings.title: Delete menu item is unreachable in the new alert-list flow because it still requires `rulerRule`
findings.body: `canDelete` is now computed as `(deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`, so it can become true purely from the new Grafana Prometheus-rule-based ability check (used when only `promRule` is supplied, as is the case for `GrafanaRuleListItem` -> `RuleActionsButtons` in the new alert list view). However the actual render condition is `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}`, and `rulerRule` is never passed in that new flow (GrafanaRuleListItem only passes `promRule`). As a result, even users with Delete permission will never see the Delete menu item for Grafana rules rendered via the new list view, even though the ability computation says they should be able to delete. This is confirmed by the new test in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx ('should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked'), which grants `AlertingRuleDelete` but asserts exactly 4 menu items (no Delete).

findings.title: Pause ability computed via promRule is dead code; can cause a stray empty divider
findings.body: `canPause` can now become true solely via the new `grafanaPauseAbility` (promRule-based) check, but the Pause menu item is still gated by `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, which is always false in the new alert-list flow because `rulerRule` is never supplied there. This means the Pause option can never actually render in that flow despite `canPause` being true, making the promRule-based pause computation effectively dead code. Worse, `canPause` still feeds into `showDivider` (`[canPause, canSilence, ..., canDuplicate].some(Boolean) && [canExport].some(Boolean)`), so when `canPause` is true but nothing else above it renders, an extra/empty `<Menu.Divider />` can appear with nothing above it in the dropdown.

findings.title: Rule view link no longer carries the `returnTo` parameter, breaking back-navigation
findings.body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx` built the rule-detail link with `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })`, where `returnTo` came from `createReturnTo()` so the detail page could navigate back to the originating list/filter view. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` builds the href as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view')` with no `returnTo` and no import of `useReturnTo`/`createReturnTo` at all. Users navigating from the alert list to a rule's detail page will lose the ability to return to their previous filtered/list view context.

findings.title: New `provenance` field on GrafanaPromRuleDTO is not confirmed to be populated by the backend
findings.body: `provenance?: string` was added to `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` and is now the sole mechanism used by `isProvisionedPromRule()` (utils/rules.ts) to flag a rule as provisioned/immutable in the new alert-list flow, replacing the previous Ruler-based provenance check (`rulerRule.grafana_alert.provenance`). This PR contains no backend changes to the Grafana Prometheus rules endpoint that would populate this field. If the backend does not actually return `provenance` in that API response, `isProvisionedPromRule` will always evaluate to false, causing provisioned (e.g. Terraform/API-managed) alert rules to be incorrectly treated as editable/deletable/duplicable from the UI, which is a data-integrity and governance risk.

findings.title: Transient 'Creating'/'Deleting' states for Grafana rules are removed without replacement
findings.body: The previous implementation fetched both the Ruler group and the Prometheus group and used `matchRules()` to show a 'Creating' indicator for rules present in the Ruler but not yet reflected by Prometheus, and a 'Deleting' indicator (via `RuleOperationListItem`) for rules still present in Prometheus after being removed from the Ruler. This PR removes the Ruler fetch and the matching logic entirely (and the corresponding `matchRules` unit tests), so during the eventual-consistency window after creating or deleting a Grafana rule, the list will simply omit or show stale rules with no visual indication of the pending state, which is a UX regression compared to the previous behavior and is not covered by any new test.
